subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning a fairly rich kitsune design: a quadruped fox body with a jaw, ears, eye decals, nine fanned tails with glowing flame tips, floating spirit flames, a shrine-style collar with tassel, a forehead mark, and gold rings, aiming for a moderately compact module around 300 lines while keeping the API correct.

Now I'm working out the actual skeleton and mesh coordinates — spine, neck, and head joint positions, then lofting the skull shape with tapering stations down to the nose, and starting on the jaw loft geometry beneath it.

Still working out the ear geometry...

Now planning the eye decals: slanted amber fox eyes with red outlines, sized and positioned on the skull, mirrored for both sides. I'm also considering adding red kumadori-style face markings as part of the eye decal.

Then I'm working out the forehead mark decal and building the body using a sweep along the spine chain, varying the radius to shape the torso, and settling on a cream-colored fur base with red markings for the kitsune look.

Now I'm deciding on the actual color scheme: a warm gold-orange coat with white chest, belly, and cheeks, and black socks on the legs, layering a countershade paint with mottling for texture. I'm also planning chest fluff using a small icosahedron shape and starting to think about the neck ruff.

For the ruff, I'm placing a ring of small spikes around the neck joint for a fluffy collar effect. Then I'm moving to leg construction, working out the root and target positions and segment lengths for a slightly bent front limb using a three-segment limb function with alternating bend directions.

Naming the four joints shoulder, elbow, wrist, and paw, tapering the radii down toward the paw and adding a flattened dark sphere for the paw tip. I'm setting up the hind leg similarly but with the knee bending forward and hock back, using a tapered radius array for a smooth sweep across the four-joint chain.

Now I'm working out the nine tails fanned out from the hip base, planning each as a three-joint chain following a catmull path spreading in a vertical fan arc, with the angle offset per tail determining the lateral and upward direction of each path point.

Adding tail taper and color gradients...

Each tail tip could get its own tint, maybe an icy blue-white for a spirit touch. For the base I'm thinking of adding a small golden ring near each tail's root using a torus shape oriented along the tangent direction, to give a decorative accent without the cost of a full sweep.

Now I'm sizing the torus rings against the tail's radius profile, settling on around 0.1 major radius with a thin 0.012 minor radius, applied across all nine tails. I'm also planning the floating spirit flames -- small glowing orbs with flame spikes on top -- scattered at mid-body heights and attached to the hips bone since they don't have a natural joint of their own. Then I'm moving on to the collar accessory, sweeping a tube around the neck with a tasseled look and a gold bell attachment.

Simplifying the bell position to a forward ray cast from the neck height instead of computing exact loop geometry. I'm also considering a forehead gem decal with red kumadori markings, and importing a shared glow kit module for the effect. Now I'm thinking through how the tail joints attach to the hips.

Adding cheek fluff spikes and a nose sphere on the head bone, skipping whiskers and mouth details. For the eyes I'm designing an SVG with a slanted almond shape, red outer swoosh, amber iris, slit pupil, and highlight, mirroring the design for left versus right sides.

Now I'm writing the sweep function for the body shape, defining the spine curve radii and color, then setting up the neck sweep radii to taper from thicker to thinner.

I'm thinking through the head coloring logic, deciding to paint the lower face and cheeks cream while keeping the rest of the coat color, and considering whether to add a decorative rune ring or halo behind the head but deciding to skip it for simplicity. Writing the hitodama flame function next...

Defining the spike geometry...
